title: Canonical module and derived operations for an exact ringed-site pullback
statement: Let $C,D$ be categories with objects in universe $u+1$, morphisms in universe $u$, essentially small in universe $u+1$, with Grothendieck topologies $J,K$. Let $R$ on $(C,J)$ and $S$ on $(D,K)$ be sheaves of commutative rings with elements in universe $u+1$. Write $\operatorname{Mod}(R),\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ for sheaves of modules in the same element universe [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\operatorname{Der}(R),\operatorname{Der}(S)$ for their ordinary unbounded derived categories with the standard localization size [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $F:C\to D$, an operation datum consists of continuity of $F$, a ring map $\varphi:R\to F_*S$ (after forgetting commutativity), a right-adjoint structure on the sectionwise module direct image $F_{*,\varphi}$, additivity of its specified left adjoint $F^*_{\varphi}$ and of $F_{*,\varphi}$, preservation of finite limits and finite colimits by $F^*_{\varphi}$, and K-injective resolutions in $\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Define $\mathrm{pullback}=F^*_{\varphi}$, $\mathrm{pushforward}=F_{*,\varphi}$, $\mathrm{left}$ to be the exact termwise pullback localized at quasi-isomorphisms, and $\mathrm{right}=RF_{*,\varphi}$ to be the ordinary K-injective right derived functor. The module adjunction is the specified canonical pullback/pushforward adjunction; the derived adjunction is its canonical exact-left/right-derived adjunction. Their units, counits, standard shifts and representative comparisons are those of these constructions. This is a definition of the datum and its associated constructions, not an assertion of existence for every continuous ringed-site map.
